segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Yeah, so quick pipeline check before the forecast call. Luma Plastics is still at $38,400 annual, 24 seats, March 1 start. I bumped the tax treatment question in the billing thread again this morning; their AP manager said the PO won't be cut until that line is in writing.

segments.speaker: Jordan
segments.text: Got it. Is that still a 12-month initial term with quarterly invoicing, or did they come back on annual upfront?

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Quarterly. They were fine with the 3% uplift in year two, no issue there. Main thing is just getting the order form to match what they saw in the quote.

segments.speaker: Jordan
segments.text: Okay. What about Harbor Ridge? That one was $62,100, right, 45 users plus the onboarding package?

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Yep, $62,100 subscription and $7,500 services. I sent deal desk the clean copy and a checking-back note after lunch; procurement has the July 31 kickoff penciled in, but they’re not routing it internally until that redline note is attached.

segments.speaker: Jordan
segments.text: Makes sense. Did security have any new asks on Harbor Ridge, or are we done with the questionnaire?

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Done. They accepted the standard SOC report and the data retention language. No custom controls, thankfully.

segments.speaker: Jordan
segments.text: Good. For Luma, do you want me to keep it in Best Case for Friday, or move it to Commit if the PO lands?

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Keep Best Case for now. If the invoice wording comes back today, I can get the customer the final PDF and maybe pull it into Friday. Otherwise it’s probably next Tuesday.
